clue.text: Writing back to university, thank God 'e's got a mark

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for writing is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
DG stands for Deo gratias, Latin for thanks be to God
the dropped-aitch 'e is just the letter E; the 's (has) is a link

explanation.surface: A Cockney writes home to college, relieved that he has passed with a decent grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MS (manuscript) into SM. DG is the Latin Deo gratias, thanks to God; 'e is 'he' with the H dropped, leaving E.
explanation.definitionFit: A smudge is a smear or blot, a dirty mark on a surface.

clue.text: Reveal the rear satellite

definitions.meaning: to bare one's buttocks as a prank or insult
a natural body orbiting a planet

explanation.definitionFit: To moon is slang for showing your bare bottom; a moon is also a body circling a planet.

clue.text: St Leger here with a fellow fly-fisher

parts.note: a don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college
an angler who casts a fly is a caster

explanation.surface: Where the famous horse race is held, alongside a man out fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: The St Leger is a classic British flat horse race run every September at a Yorkshire racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The racecourse town that hosts the St Leger, oldest of Britain's classic horse races, is a description of the place.

clue.text: Cabinet oil expert outing the French 22

indicators.note: outing means exposing something concealed, so the letters sit concealed inside these words

explanation.surface: A government minister who knows about oil is publicly exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 refers to the answer at 22-down, a heavenly body that twinkles at night; the clue wants the French word for it, concealed in cabinET OIL Expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Étoile is the French noun for the twinkling body in the night sky that 22-down names in English.

clue.text: Winner bagged first place in this

definitions.text: Winner bagged first place in this

parts.words: Winner bagged first place in this
parts.note: sounds like a sporting triumph, but literally the winner was inside a bag when coming first, as in the school sports-day event with hopping in sacks

explanation.definitionFit: A school sports-day race in which competitors hop along with their legs inside sacks is literally won by someone in a bag.

clue.text: Unite in mess of mess; hang together roughly or, in unison, belt out 2 21, 9, 11, 19 21, 22 13, 23, say, or 26 boy

definitions.text: in unison, belt out 2 21, 9, 11, 19 21, 22 13, 23, say, or 26 boy
definitions.meaning: the cross-references spell song titles: Moon River, Downtown, All of a Sudden, Old Man River, Stardust, Who Is Silvia and Nature Boy, sung together by a choir

indicators.note: roughly means in a rough, untidy fashion, so the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A muddled instruction to a choir to pull together and belt out a medley of famous songs.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is 'in mess of mess hang together', 24 letters, rearranged by 'roughly'. The tail is a second, literal definition: a choir singing those songs in unison from one printed sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to agree or present a united view, literally all singers reading identical words.

clue.text: Monastic London characters in the Lake District

indicators.note: characters are letters, here the letters of the two words taken as raw material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Monks from London turn up among the lakes and fells of Cumbria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' signals that the letters of MONASTIC LONDON are rearranged into a three-word mountain name. The Lake District is a mountainous national park in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This fell is a well-known peak above the village and lake of the same first name in Cumbria's Lake District.

clue.text: Swift attack capturing prince

indicators.note: capturing means one word holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: A lightning assault seizes a member of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and swift are adjectival synonyms for very fast.

clue.text: Reprimand night flyer for attacking Brussels?

parts.note: to carpet someone is to call them in for a telling-off
a moth is an insect that flies at night

explanation.surface: Telling off a night-time pilot for bombing the Belgian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Brussels is not the city but a kind of carpet; the larvae of this insect eat woollen rugs.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect's larvae devour woollen floor coverings, of which Brussels weave is one kind, so it is the creature that attacks them.

clue.text: Americans doing the business here in Bangor, say?

definitions.meaning: in US usage the central business district of a city
Bangor in Northern Ireland is a town in County Down

explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a city's commercial centre by this name; split, it also describes any town in County Down, such as Bangor.

clue.text: Never admitting training in household textiles

indicators.note: admitting means letting the second piece in, inside the first

parts.note: nary is a dialect word for never or not a single
PE is physical education, training of the body

explanation.surface: A household that refuses to allow any exercise near its linen cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Never' is the dialect word nary, as in 'nary a word'; 'admitting' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Napery is an old word for household linen, especially tablecloths and napkins.

clue.text: Strangely, 'e found Dallas immediately

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so these letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: the dropped-aitch 'e is just the letter E

explanation.surface: Someone, oddly, stumbled on the Texan city right away.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means suddenly or without warning, an adverbial equivalent of at once.

clue.text: The Bundesbank's dream of continental coverage?

definitions.text: The Bundesbank's dream of continental coverage?

parts.words: The Bundesbank's dream of continental coverage?
parts.note: a German central banker's dream is a vision of the single European currency; the whole is also the song contest broadcast across Europe

explanation.definitionFit: The annual song contest broadcast across the continent splits into the European currency and a dream or vision.

clue.text: It becomes us all and, ungrammatically, on the contrary!

definitions.text: It becomes us all and, ungrammatically, on the contrary!

parts.words: It becomes us all and, ungrammatically, on the contrary!
parts.note: we all return to this at death (ashes to ashes), so it becomes us and we, ungrammatically 'us', become it

explanation.definitionFit: The burial service says we return to powdery earth, so in death we all become it and it becomes us.

clue.text: Work with large numbers of tree dwellers

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
OS is outsize, a large clothing size
sums are arithmetic problems with numbers

explanation.surface: Counting a huge population of animals living in the trees is a big job.
explanation.definitionFit: These American marsupials live largely in trees, so they are tree dwellers.

clue.text: See 5
Man without home thanks one for support

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first word goes round the rest

parts.note: taken as written
in means at home
ta is British informal for thank you
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A homeless man grateful to anyone who will back him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. TA is everyday British for thanks; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain someone is to support them financially or keep them going.

clue.text: Barber's harmony loud, so far as we are concerned

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud

parts.words: so far as we are concerned
parts.note: 'for our part' means so far as we are concerned; the phrase supplies our part

explanation.surface: Barbershop singers announce they are, for their part, singing loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbershop singing is unaccompanied close harmony for a quartet of male voices.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbershop quartets sing in harmony split between four voices, each taking one line.

clue.text: No further charge on the Blaydon Races?

parts.note: Blaydon is on Tyneside in north-east England, NE
the TT, the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy, is a famous set of motorcycle races

explanation.surface: Free entry to a famous Tyneside horse-racing day celebrated in a Geordie song.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blaydon Races is a Geordie folk song about a race meeting near Newcastle. A nett sum is what remains after deductions, with nothing more to take off.
explanation.definitionFit: A nett price or amount is final, with no further deduction or charge to be made.

clue.text: See 6
Declines more treatment with such instruments

indicators.note: treatment of the letters means processing them into a new order, fitting a clinic

explanation.surface: A skincare clinic turns down extra procedures that use particular tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges DECLINES MORE; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: These tiny needles are cosmetic instruments used in skin treatment, so 'such instruments' points to them via the treatment in the clue.

clue.text: Banker with a bank in Paris, right?

parts.note: rive is French for a riverbank, as in the Rive Gauche

explanation.surface: A financier with an account at a Parisian bank checks he is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is not a financier but something that has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowing watercourse has banks on either side, so it is crosswordese 'banker'.

clue.text: 4's raising the population of Hamelin

indicators.note: raising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: the Pied Piper legend tells of Hamelin overrun by rats

explanation.surface: The Pied Piper's town and its vermin are being lifted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 4's points to the answer at 4-down, the French word whose English equivalent this is.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer at 4-down is French for a heavenly body; this is the English word it translates.

clue.text: One's turning left through her!

indicators.note: turning means the short phrase is read the other way round

parts.note: one's, read as one is, gives I plus S
via means by way of, through

explanation.surface: Someone spins round, turns left and passes right through a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses IS to SI. 'her' refers to Who Is Silvia?, one of the songs listed at 5-down.
explanation.definitionFit: This woman's name is the 'her' of Schubert's song Who Is Silvia?, set from Shakespeare, so the pronoun stands for her.

clue.text: Supports weapons without support

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word sits around the other

parts.note: arms are weapons
a rest is a support, as for a snooker cue

explanation.surface: Military aid in weaponry offered with no other help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking; the plural definition matches the plural answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sides of a chair on which you lay your forearms are supports for them.

clue.text: In French, spell "Charm"

parts.note: en is French for in
a trance is a spellbound state

explanation.surface: A French phrase meaning to cast a spell of charm.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the verb: to enchant someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone, stressed on the second syllable, is to charm or enchant them.

clue.text: Innate, primitive disposition!

parts.note: describes one's inborn character, and also the primitive wild world

explanation.definitionFit: A person's inborn character or temperament is their essential make-up, untouched by nurture.
